Adding a few technical details for the test plan so Acme's infra team can prepare:

Test harness notes (short):
- Use our testrunner (docker image) that drives parallel client threads and reports per-request metrics. We'll provision a dedicated GPU pool and a small routing layer to reproduce realistic queuing.
- Workload mix: 70% short prompts (~64 tokens), 30% long prompts (~512 tokens). We'll replay sample-workload.json you provided.
- Concurrency scenarios:
  * Burst: 5s spike windows at +3x baseline traffic every 60s for 30 minutes.
  * Steady-state: constant arrival process for 1 hour per concurrency level.
- Metrics captured: token TTFT, generation p50/p95/p99, request queue depth, average GPU utilization, and tail latencies when KV cache hits/misses occur.

Preliminary rate-limit tuning plan:
- Set a soft concurrency cap per frontend at 120 concurrent requests, with token-bucket burst allowance of 60 tokens/sec for short spikes.
- Introduce per-account concurrency reservation for critical paths (canary traffic).

If Acme can provision monitoring access to a staging endpoint we will stream metrics to the shared Drive folder.

Subject: Re: MAP request: performance evaluation & close timeline — test results

Hi all —

We completed the concurrency sweep on 2026-05-21 and collected the requested metrics. Summary highlights (see attached CSV and graphs):
- TTFT (512-token prompts): p50 = 132 ms, p95 = 318 ms, p99 = 645 ms.
- Sustained throughput (steady-state): 210 rps with average GPU utilization 64% (model: open-llama-70B-quant).
- Burst behavior: at injected spikes up to 800 rps we observed a queue depth increase and p95 spikes above 1.2s when concurrent inbound > 140 per frontend.
- Queueing knee: consistent latency degradation once per-frontend concurrency exceeded ~120 requests; queue length grew linearly and then requests experienced 429s (rate-limited) under the current soft cap.
- Recommended tuning enacted in the final run: soft concurrency cap = 120, hard reject at 180, token-bucket burst allowance = 80 tokens/sec. With those settings, burst p95 reduced to 520 ms and fewer 429s occurred.

Action items from these runs:
1) We recommend reserving a Dedicated pool sized for sustained 200 rps with headroom (2x) for bursts; that maps to our standard Dedicated configuration D2 (4 GPUs).
2) For the frontend, implement the soft concurrency cap and token-bucket burst allowance above; enable a circuit-breaker that returns 503 for requests that would queue beyond a 2s threshold.
3) We'll prepare a formal failure-mode table and a runbook for retry/backoff behavior.

Attachments: performance-results-2026-05-20.csv, latency-graphs-2026-05-20.pdf

Jonas Weber
